california.question: Drivers trapped behind a slow-moving vehicle often:

options.B: Allow the vehicle plenty of space.
options.C: Are happy with the speed of travel.

california.explanation: It is common for drivers to tailgate slow-moving vehicles that cannot keep up with the speed of surrounding traffic. If you are being tailgated, allow the other driver to pass your vehicle.

california.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:
california.explanation: It is important to inspect your tires before every drive. Rust around wheel nuts may indicate that they are loose.

california.question: Mirrors should be checked:

options.B: When changing lanes, but only when other vehicles are nearby.
options.C: When changing lanes, but only if it is dark outside.

california.explanation: Always check for traffic in your mirrors before changing lanes. Frequent mirror checks should be a part of your normal scanning routine.

california.question: To apply for a CDL, an applicant must be at least:
california.explanation: In California, you must be at least 18 years old to apply for a commercial driver license.

california.question: If you’re unfamiliar with the area in which you must back up, you should:

options.A: Get out of your vehicle and walk around the area to become more familiar with it.
options.B: Not use both side mirrors because it can be distracting.
options.C: Wait for someone else to back up in the area so you can see how they do it.

california.explanation: Before backing up, you should get out of your vehicle and look at your line of travel. Check your clearance to the sides and overhead.

california.question: A ____ allows a driver to gradually apply spring brakes.
california.explanation: A modulating control valve allows a driver to gradually apply spring brakes. In equipped vehicles, the valve is controlled by a lever located on the dashboard.

california.question: Cargo should have one tie-down for every ____ of cargo.
california.explanation: Cargo should be restrained by at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. However, all cargo should have at least two tie-downs, no matter the size of the cargo.

california.question: When stopping a manual transmission vehicle, you should:

options.A: Push the clutch in when the engine is close to idle.
options.B: Push the clutch out when the engine is close to idle.
options.C: Shift into neutral when the engine is close to idle.

california.explanation: When stopping, apply gradual pressure to the brake pedal and stop smoothly. If stopping a manual transmission vehicle, push the clutch in when the engine is close to idle.

california.question: Poor weight balance:

options.C: Increases a driver’s ability to steer.

california.explanation: Poorly balanced loads can lead to unsafe handling. It is important to properly distribute the weight of cargo when loading a vehicle.

california.question: One way to prevent hydroplaning on wet road surfaces is to:

options.A: Ensure that your tires have good tread depth.

california.explanation: When driving on a wet road surface, the risk of hydroplaning is increased if your tire pressure is too low or your tire tread is too worn. If you begin to hydroplane, release the accelerator and push in the clutch to slow down.

california.question: Which of the following is the best advice for driving in fog?

options.A: Try not to drive in fog.

california.explanation: Driving in fog is always dangerous and should be avoided entirely if at all possible. If you must drive in fog, be sure to turn on your low beam headlights and fog lights, even during the daytime.

california.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.B: Get out of the vehicle and call for assistance.
options.C: Continue trying to get your vehicle off the tracks until you are successful.

california.explanation: If your CMV gets stuck on railroad tracks, you should immediately leave the vehicle and get away from the tracks. Check the signposts or signal housing at the crossing for emergency contact information and call 911, or another appropriate emergency number.

california.question: If the low pressure warning signal activates while you are driving, you should:

options.B: Exit the road and park as soon as safely possible.
options.C: Stop where you are and park.

california.explanation: If the low pressure warning signal activates while you are driving, it is important that you safely exit the roadway as soon as possible and park your vehicle. If the air pressure gets too low, the brakes will no longer work well enough for you to stop safely.

california.question: If you must drive in reverse, using driver's side backing:

options.C: Is only recommended if it is raining.

california.explanation: If you must back up, it is safest to back toward the driver's side of the vehicle. This way, as the driver, you will have the best possible view of your path of travel.

california.question: Regrooved tires are:

options.A: Allowed only on the front of a bus.
options.B: Allowed only on the rear of a bus.
options.C: Not allowed anywhere on a bus.

california.explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires are not permitted to be used on the front of a bus.

california.question: What do air brakes use to make the brakes work?
california.explanation: Many large CMVs are equipped with air brakes. An air braking system uses compressed air to operate.

california.question: As part of the vehicle inspection test, you will be asked to:

options.A: Explain what you would inspect and why.

california.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be required to do a complete inspection of your vehicle. During this inspection, you must explain to the examiner what you are inspecting and why you are inspecting those items.

california.question: If you are disqualified from driving:

options.A: Your employer will be notified by the state.
options.B: You must notify your employer within two business days.
options.C: You must notify your employer within a month.

california.explanation: You must notify your employer within two business days if your license is suspended, revoked, or canceled, or if you are otherwise disqualified from driving.

california.question: If there is a fire in your vehicle, you should not:

options.A: Park in an area away from buildings, trees, brush, and other vehicles.
options.C: Notify emergency services of your problem and your location.

california.explanation: In the event of a vehicle fire, you should leave the road and stop in an open area. Do not pull into a service station as fuels at the service station could catch fire. Report the fire and your location to emergency services.

california.question: Driving at night is:

options.A: Safer than driving during the day.
options.B: Just as safe as driving during the day.
options.C: More dangerous than driving during the day.

california.explanation: Driving at night is more dangerous than driving during the day because hazards become more difficult to see in the dark.

california.question: To avoid a hazard, you:

options.A: Should always come to a complete stop.
options.B: May need to swerve your vehicle out of the way.

california.explanation: Stopping is not always the best way to avoid a hazard. If there is not enough space for you to stop to avoid coming into contact with the hazard, swerving out of the way may be your safest option.

california.question: When driving in fog, you should:
california.explanation: It is best not to avoid driving in fog. However, if you must drive under foggy conditions, be sure to decrease your speed.

california.question: Talking on a cell phone while driving removes about ____ of a person's focus from the task of driving.
california.explanation: Distracted driving is always dangerous. Talking on a cell phone takes away about 39 percent of a person's mental energy that would otherwise be devoted to driving.

california.question: What must be on all air tanks with air-braked vehicles?
california.explanation: All air tanks on air-braked vehicles must have a check valve located between the air compressor and the first reservoir. The valve allows air to flow in only one direction and helps keep air from leaving the air compressor if the compressor develops a leak.

california.question: When changing lanes, turn signals:

options.B: Should only be used if a vehicle is close to you.

california.explanation: Always signal your intentions before turning or changing lanes. Do not assume that other drivers will move out of your way simply because you are signaling to turn.

california.question: How should you brake if your vehicle's ABS is not working?

options.A: Brake normally, as you will still have functioning brakes.
options.C: Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

california.explanation: Without a working Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), your vehicle will still have normal brake function. Continue to drive and brake as you normally would and have your ABS serviced as soon as possible.

california.question: During an inspection, slack adjusters on S-cam brakes should not move more than:
california.explanation: Check each slack adjuster after parking on level ground, setting wheel chocks, and disengaging the parking brake. Pull the slack adjusters to make sure they do not move more than about one inch from where the push rod is attached. If they move more than one inch, they may be out of adjustment and will need to be fixed.

california.question: When starting your vehicle, the coolant temperature should:

options.C: Quickly jump from low to high.

california.explanation: Watch the gauges in your vehicle before starting a trip. After starting your vehicle's engine, the coolant temperature should begin a gradual rise to the normal operating range.

california.question: Some air brake systems introduce alcohol into the system to:

options.A: Make the brakes work without squeaking.
options.B: Prevent ice from forming in the brake system.
options.C: Prevent people from breathing the air from the system.

california.explanation: Some air brake systems contain an alcohol evaporator. An evaporator introduces alcohol into the system to help inhibit the formation of ice in cold weather.

california.question: If you are taking the driving test and the route does not include a railroad crossing, you:

options.A: Will not have to do anything related to a crossing.
options.B: May have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
options.C: Will have to take a different route.

california.explanation: During the on-road driving test, if your route does not include a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and demonstrate the necessary procedures at a simulated location.

california.question: Always perform the steps of a pre-trip inspection in the same order each time because:

options.A: You will be less likely to forget something.
options.B: You will have more time to complete the inspection.

california.explanation: Completing the steps of a vehicle inspection in the same order before every trip aids in learning what the proper steps are. Additionally, you be less likely to forget a step when going through the checklist in a prescribed order.

california.question: If a tire fails, you should:
california.explanation: Braking after a tire fails can result in a loss of control. Stay off your brakes, if possible, until your vehicle has slowed considerably.

california.question: During an applied leakage test, the maximum leakage rate for a double combination vehicle is:
california.explanation: It is important to know the maximum air loss rate that is safe for your specific vehicle. A double combination vehicle should have a leakage rate no higher than 4 psi in a minute during an applied leakage test.

california.question: During the driving test, the examiner will be scoring you on:

options.B: How quickly you arrive to your destination.

california.explanation: During the on-road driving test, the examiner will be scoring you on specific driving maneuvers, as well as your general driving behavior.

california.question: If your brakes fail while you are traveling downhill and there is no available escape ramp, you should:
california.explanation: If your brakes fail while you are driving downhill, you should first look for an escape ramp to stop your vehicle. If no ramp is available, you should look for an alternative place to bring your vehicle to a stop, such as an open field or side road that flattens out or turns uphill.

california.question: You may not consume alcohol within ____ of going on duty.
california.explanation: Commercial vehicle drivers are prohibited from consuming any intoxicating beverage, regardless of its alcohol content, within four hours of going on duty.

california.question: Do not operate a vehicle if any brake drums have cracks that are larger than ____ of the width of the friction area.
california.explanation: Before beginning a trip, it is important to check the brake drums during your walk-around inspection. It is unsafe to drive if any brake drum has a crack more than one half of the width of the friction area.

california.question: The radiator cap:

options.A: Should not be removed when the coolant is hot.
options.B: Can be removed when the coolant is hot.
options.C: Should be cool to the touch under normal driving conditions.

california.explanation: Never remove the radiator cap or any part of the pressurized cooling system until it has cooled. Opening the cap while the system is too hot could release steam and boiling water that could severely burn you. If the radiator cap is cool to the touch, the system is likely cool enough for you to open the cap.

california.question: When should a driver sign a vehicle inspection report?
california.explanation: You must sign a vehicle inspection report only if defects were noted and either certified to have been repaired or certified as not needing to be repaired.

california.question: During an applied leakage test, the maximum leakage rate for a double combination vehicle is ____ in a minute.
california.explanation: It is important to know the maximum air loss rate that is safe for your specific vehicle. A double combination vehicle should have a leakage rate no higher than 4 psi in a minute during an applied leakage test.

california.question: A person driving with an open window in cold weather may be:

options.B: A person who is dressed inappropriately.
options.C: A person who likes fresh air.

california.explanation: It is important to observe other drivers' actions and identify clues that a person could be driving impaired. Drivers who have had too much to drink, are sleepy, are on drugs, or are ill can present hazards to other drivers. One sign that a driver may be impaired is that they have their windows rolled down in cold weather.

california.question: What is removed when an air tank is drained?
california.explanation: In an air brake system, air tanks have drains to remove accumulations of water and compressor oil. Allowing water and oil to accumulate in the system could cause damage to the brakes.

california.question: The ____ tells a driver how much pressure is in the air tanks.
california.explanation: A vehicle that is equipped with air brakes must also be equipped with a supply pressure gauge. This gauge tells the driver how much air pressure is in each of the vehicle's air tanks.

california.question: Containerized loads are used:

options.A: When the cargo is too large to fit on a truck.
options.B: When the cargo has been or will be transported by a train.
options.C: When the cargo is a liquid.

california.explanation: Containerized loads are generally used when freight is carried partway by rail or ship. Sealed materials cannot be inspected, but a driver should ensure that the containers do not exceed safe and legal weight limits.

california.question: If being tailgated, you should:

options.B: Increase the amount of space between your vehicle and the vehicle in front of you.

california.explanation: If you are being tailgated, you should increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead of you. This reduces the need for you to make sudden changes in speed or direction while making it easier for the tailgater to pass your vehicle.

california.question: Violation points for major violations are retained on a driving record for:
california.explanation: Points for major violations that occur while driving a commercial motor vehicle, or while you are a CDL holder, will be retained on your record for 55 years.

california.question: When completing a driver's side parallel parking maneuver, you should:

options.A: Pull forward directly into the parking space.
options.B: Back up past the parking space, then pull forward into it.
options.C: Pull forward past the parking space, then back into it.

california.explanation: You may be asked to complete a parallel parking maneuver into a parking space that is to the left of your vehicle. You should drive past the parking space before backing into it while bringing the rear of your vehicle as close to the rear of the space as possible. Your vehicle should be completely within the boundaries of the space.

california.question: While operating on a downgrade, you should brake until you reach a speed that is:
california.explanation: While driving downhill, you should hold down the brake pedal until your vehicle reaches a speed 5 mph below your safe speed, then release the brake pedal. Repeat this process.

california.question: If unable to tell if the road is becoming icy and slippery, a driver:

options.B: May open their window and feel the front of the side mirror for ice.
options.C: Should look at the road closely.

california.explanation: If you think the road surface may be becoming icy but you are not certain, you can open your window and feel the front of the side mirror, mirror support, or antenna. If ice has formed on any of these items, the road is likely becoming icy as well.

california.question: When parking, you should not use the parking brake if:

options.C: There is snow on the ground.

california.explanation: If your brakes are hot after coming down a steep grade, you should not use your parking brake when parking. Let your brakes cool before applying the parking brake or risk damaging the brakes.

california.question: To prevent a vehicle from rolling backward when beginning to move forward from a stopped position, you should:
california.explanation: To prevent a vehicle with manual transmission from rolling backward when you begin to move forward from a stopped position, you can partly engage the clutch before removing your foot from the brake pedal.

california.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, a look is when:

options.A: A driver checks the gauges on their instrument panel.
options.B: A driver checks their blind spots.
options.C: A driver walks to the back of their vehicle to check its position.

california.explanation: A driver uses a look when they open their door, leave their seated position, and walk to the back of the vehicle to check its position. During the straight line backing exercise, a driver may not exceed one look. During any other exercise, a driver may not exceed two looks.

california.question: Having ABS on only one axle:

options.B: Still allows you additional control when braking.
options.C: Slows the vehicle, but cannot stop it.

california.explanation: If you have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) equipped on only the tractor, only the trailer, or only one axle, you will still have more control over the vehicle when braking than you would without ABS. You should brake normally.

california.question: If the spring brakes are on, you should:
california.explanation: Do not use the brake pedal when the spring brakes are on. This could damage the brakes by subjecting them to the combined forces of springs and air pressure.

california.question: What is road rage?

options.A: Operating a motor vehicle with the intent of doing harm to others
options.B: Operating a motor vehicle that is deemed unsafe
options.C: Operating a motor vehicle that has not been inspected

california.explanation: Aggressive driving is defined as operating a motor vehicle in a selfish, bold, or pushy manner. Road rage is defined as operating a motor vehicle with the intent of doing harm to others, or the intent of physically assaulting another driver or their vehicle.

california.question: A modulating control valve can control the:
california.explanation: A modulating control valve allows a driver to gradually apply spring brakes. In equipped vehicles, the valve is controlled by a lever located on the dashboard.

california.question: Vehicles equipped with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have ____ malfunction lamps to indicate when the ABS is not working.
california.explanation: Vehicles with ABS have yellow malfunction lamps to alert drivers when the braking systems are not working. Be sure you know where the malfunction lamp on your vehicle is before beginning a trip.

california.question: If turning to avoid a hazard:

options.B: You should not brake as it may cause the wheels to lock.

california.explanation: You should not brake while making a quick turn to avoid a hazard. Doing so could cause your wheels to lock and make your vehicle skid out of control.

california.question: When adjusting your mirrors before a trip:

options.A: No part of your vehicle should be visible in any mirror.
options.B: Part of your vehicle should be visible in the mirrors.
options.C: More than half of each mirror should show the vehicle.

california.explanation: When properly adjusted, your mirrors should each display some part of your vehicle. Being able to see your own vehicle in your mirrors will give you a point of reference when judging the positions of other objects.

california.question: When traveling down a steep grade, you switch into a lower gear:

options.B: When you have already started the grade.
options.C: As far down the grade as possible.

california.explanation: You should shift your vehicle's transmission into a low gear before staring a downhill grade. Be prepared for gravity to increase your vehicle's speed when traveling downhill.

california.question: Braking mechanisms are located inside:
california.explanation: Drum brakes are attached to the wheels and located on the axles of a vehicle. The braking mechanisms that cause the vehicle to stop can be found inside of a drum brake.

california.question: Driving with a cargo of hanging meat in a trailer:

options.A: Is discouraged during the summer months.
options.B: Can be problematic because animals are attracted to the smell of the meat.
options.C: Is challenging because the load has a high center of gravity.

california.explanation: An operator should drive with care when transporting a cargo of hanging meat. Such a load is unstable, both because it has a high center of gravity and because the swinging of the meat can affect the driver's handling of the vehicle.

california.question: Mirror adjustment can only be checked properly if:

options.C: The vehicle is on a slight incline.

california.explanation: On a vehicle with one or more trailers, mirror adjustment can only be checked accurately if the trailers are straight. Mirror adjustment should be checked before the start of every trip.

california.question: You should maintain at least ____ of following distance per every 10 feet of your vehicle when you are traveling more slowly than 40 mph.
california.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, you should allow at least one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. Follow the same formula when traveling at faster speeds, then add one additional second to your following distance. Remember that larger vehicles require more space to stop than smaller vehicles.

california.question: How can you check for a leak in hydraulic brakes?

options.A: Pump the brake pedal three times, then hold down the pedal for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
options.B: Push the brake pedal down as far as possible and release. If the brake pedal returns to its normal position, there may be a problem.
options.C: Push the brake pedal down as far as possible and release. If the brake squeaks, there may be a problem.

california.explanation: Check hydraulic brakes by pumping the brake pedal three times before applying firm pressure to the pedal for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it does, there may be a leak or some other problem in the braking system.

california.question: A tread depth of ____ should be in every major groove of a tire that is not in the front of a commercial motor vehicle.
california.explanation: For safe operation, a commercial motor vehicle needs a tread depth of 4/32 of an inch in every major groove on the front tires, and a tread depth of 2/32 of an inch on other tires.

california.question: Why do large vehicles use air brakes?

options.A: Other brake systems squeak too loudly.
options.B: Air brakes are very effective systems.
options.C: Other braking systems are hard to come by.

california.explanation: If used and maintained properly, air brakes are a safe and effective way to stop large, heavy vehicles.

california.question: When backing with a trailer, you should begin by:

options.A: Turning the steering wheel in the direction of the turn.
options.B: Turning the steering wheel in the direction opposite of the turn.
options.C: Turning the wheel as sharply as possible.

california.explanation: When backing with a trailer, begin by turning the steering wheel in the direction opposite of the turn. Once the trailer starts to turn, reverse the direction of the steering wheel to follow the trailer.

california.question: While driving downhill, you should brake until you reach a speed that is ____ below your safe speed, then release the brake pedal.
california.explanation: While driving downhill, you should hold down the brake pedal until your vehicle reaches a speed 5 mph below your safe speed, then release the brake pedal. Repeat this process.

california.question: When backing with a trailer:

options.A: You should not back up in a straight line.
options.B: You should not correct drift until you are far off course.
options.C: You should frequently pull forward to reposition the vehicle.

california.explanation: When backing, you should pull forward to reposition your vehicle whenever needed. Drift should be corrected immediately by turning the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.

california.question: If involved in an accident, which of the following is not recommended?

options.A: Trying to move your vehicle to the side of the road

california.explanation: When involved in an accident, you should protect the area, notify authorities, care for the injured, collect required information, and report the accident. You can lose your license for leaving the scene of an accident.

california.question: When leaving your vehicle:

options.A: The air brakes should be applied.
options.B: The parking brake should be applied.
options.C: Brakes should not be applied if the vehicle is left out of gear.

california.explanation: Parking brakes should be used whenever you park. If necessary, chock your wheels.

california.question: When backing up, follow a turning trailer by:

options.A: Changing nothing. The vehicle will naturally follow the trailer.
options.B: Changing the direction of the steering wheel.
options.C: Turning the steering wheel even harder in the direction that it is already turning.

california.explanation: When backing with a trailer, begin by turning the steering wheel in the direction opposite of the turn. Once the trailer starts to turn, reverse the direction of the steering wheel to follow the trailer.

california.question: By beginning a left turn before reaching the center of an intersection, you:

options.A: Will likely complete the turn satisfactorily.
options.B: May hit other vehicles with the left side of your vehicle.
options.C: Can expect other drivers to move their vehicles to accommodate your turn.

california.explanation: When planning to turn left at an intersection, make sure you have reached the center of the intersection before beginning the turn. If you turn too soon, off-tracking may cause the left side of your vehicle to hit another vehicle.

california.question: Cargo with a high center of gravity:

options.A: Can make a vehicle likely to tip over.

california.explanation: Cargo with a high center of gravity makes a vehicle more likely to tip over than cargo with a low center of gravity. For this reason, it is important that the weight of cargo be distributed as low as possible.

california.question: When driving in winter, which of the following should receive extra attention in a pre-trip inspection?
california.explanation: When doing a pre-trip inspection during the winter, you should pay extra attention to the coolant level and amount of antifreeze; the defrosting and heating equipment; the wiper blades and windshield washer; the tires and tire chains; the lights and reflectors; the windows and mirrors; the hand holds, steps, and deck plates; the radiator shuttles and winterfront; and exhaust system.

california.question: When braking with ABS, you should:

options.C: Brake harder than you would with a different braking system.

california.explanation: When braking a vehicle equipped with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you should not brake any differently than you would if driving a vehicle with a different braking system.

california.question: A truck tractor built after March 1, 1997 must be equipped with:
california.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 are required to be equipped with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

california.question: A pre-trip inspection should include:

options.A: A check of the engine oil level.

california.explanation: When examining the engine compartment during a pre-trip inspection, you should check the engine oil level, the radiator coolant level, and the condition of the hoses.

california.question: Rough acceleration:

options.A: Is a good way to stay awake on long trips.

california.explanation: Rough acceleration can cause mechanical damage, so be sure to accelerate smoothly and gradually.

california.question: If you are being tailgated while driving a large vehicle, do all of the following, except:
california.explanation: If you find yourself being tailgated by another driver, you should increase your following distance and avoid making quick moves. Increasing your speed may only result in the other driver continuing to tailgate you at a higher speed. Do not turn on your taillights or flash your brake lights at the other driver.

california.question: If an unusual noise or feeling occurs in a vehicle while it is being driven, the driver should:

options.A: Assume it is not a concern and continue driving.
options.B: Hope the vehicle does alright until it is switched to another driver.
options.C: Check the situation to determine the proper solution.

california.explanation: If you see, hear, smell, or feel anything while driving that does not feel right, you should have it checked out.

california.question: When driving, you should stop every ____ to take a break to avoid becoming too tired.
california.explanation: To reduce the risk of becoming fatigued on a long trip, you should stop to take a break at least once for every two hours or 100 miles driven.

california.question: If asked by a law enforcement officer to take a test to determine your blood alcohol concentration (BAC):

options.A: You can refuse to take the test without a penalty.
options.B: You can refuse taking the test but will be required to pay a $50 fine.
options.C: You will lose your CDL if you refuse to take the test.

california.explanation: Most states have an Implied Consent Law, which means that by driving a vehicle on the state's roads, you have agreed to undergo a drug or alcohol test if a police officer asks you to do so. If you refuse to submit to a test, you will lose your operating privileges. Make sure you are aware of the laws for every state in which you drive.

california.question: Pre-trip inspections are:

options.B: Needed only for trips longer than 100 miles in length.

california.explanation: Federal and state laws require drivers to inspect their vehicles before every trip, regardless of length.

california.question: If you realize you may be running late to your destination, you should:

options.C: Deal with it and drive at a safe speed.

california.explanation: To reduce the risk of developing aggressive driving behavior, you should take measures to manage your stress. One strategy to do this is to simply take a deep breath and accept your circumstances if you realize you will be late to your destination.

california.question: In hot weather, spots on the pavement where tar is bleeding:

options.B: Offer the same amount of traction as the rest of the roadway.
options.C: Offer more traction than the rest of the roadway.

california.explanation: Tar in road pavement often rises to the surface of the road, or "bleeds," in very hot weather. Watch for such areas because they can be very slippery.

california.question: If driving on a surface with poor traction, a driver should accelerate slowly:

options.A: Because it is always good to accelerate slowly.
options.B: To keep from losing control of the vehicle.
options.C: So that they do not accelerate faster than the vehicle ahead.

california.explanation: To avoid a loss of control, you should accelerate slowly when driving in poor-traction conditions, such as rain or snow.

california.question: An Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR) does not need to include which of the following?
california.explanation: An Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR) must include information about the distance traveled by a vehicle and the amount of fuel purchased. The required distance information includes the dates of a trip and the total distance traveled by the vehicle.

california.question: When trying to put out an electrical fire, you should:
california.explanation: B:C fire extinguishers are designed to work on electrical fires and burning liquids. Don't pour water on an electrical fire.

california.question: Wheels with welding repairs are:

options.A: Safe to be used if the repairs were done by a professional.
options.B: Safe to be used if the repair seems solid.

california.explanation: Wheels or rims that have had welding repairs are not safe for use. They should be replaced before the vehicle is taken on the road.

california.question: A poor balance of weight in a trailer:
california.explanation: Poorly balanced weight in a trailer can make handling unsafe. For example, either too little or too much weight on the front axle can make a vehicle difficult to steer. Weight should be distributed evenly from front to back and from side to side. It should be distributed as low as possible.

california.question: What is a tire load?

options.A: The minimum safe weight a tire can carry
options.B: The maximum safe weight a tire can carry

california.explanation: Tire load is defined as the maximum safe weight that a tire can carry at a specified pressure.

california.question: Cargo being transported should be checked:

options.B: Before the trip and again within the first 50 miles of the trip.

california.explanation: Cargo should be inspected before beginning a trip, within the first 50 miles of the trip, and every three hours or 150 miles traveled thereafter. Cargo should be inspected every time the driver stops to take a break. The driver of a truck transporting cargo is responsible for the cargo being safely secured throughout the trip.

california.question: If driving through flowing water or a large puddle, you should:

options.C: Try to stop in the water.

california.explanation: It is best to avoid driving through large puddles or moving water. If there is no way to avoid driving through water, you should slow down, shift into a low gear, and gently apply the brakes. Pressing linings against the brake drums or discs will keep water, mud, silt, and sand from getting inside the brake mechanisms.

california.question: When operating a vehicle with a dual air brake system, the driver should:

options.A: Let the vehicle warm up before driving to ensure that the fuel reaches the engine.
options.B: Let the air compressor build up a minimum of 100 psi pressure in the primary and secondary systems before driving.
options.C: Begin driving just after the vehicle starts.

california.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, allow time for the air compressor to build up a minimum of 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems. Watch the air pressure gauges to monitor the pressure levels.

california.question: When exiting a vehicle, it is important to maintain ____ with your vehicle at all times.
california.explanation: As you exit your vehicle during the basic vehicle control skills test, you must face the vehicle and maintain three points of contact at all times. If your testing vehicle is a bus, you must maintain contact with the handrail. Exiting the vehicle incorrectly may result in automatic failure of the basic control skills test.

california.question: In a vehicle with dual air brakes, a leak in one system ____ the second system.
california.explanation: A dual air brake system is made up of two separate air brake systems. If there is an air leak in one system, it may not affect the other.

california.question: When loading a trailer, weight should be:

options.C: Placed as far to the left as possible.

california.explanation: Cargo with a high center of gravity makes a vehicle more likely to tip over than cargo with a low center of gravity. For this reason, it is important that the weight of cargo be distributed as low as possible.

california.question: Texting while driving is especially dangerous because:

options.A: It is both a mental and physical distraction.
options.B: A message may be upsetting to the driver.
options.C: People like to read and may become too engaged in their phones.

california.explanation: Texting while driving is particularly dangerous because it is both a mental and physical distraction to the driver. In addition to diverting a driver's mental attention away from the road, texting requires a person to remove at least one hand from the vehicle's controls.

california.question: When leaving a vehicle unattended, a driver should:

options.B: Only set the parking brake if the vehicle is parked on a slope.

california.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when leaving your vehicle unattended.

california.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
california.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997, and other vehicles with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1998, must be equipped with anti-lock brakes.

california.question: When completing an offset back/left parking maneuver, a driver should:

options.A: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
options.B: Drive straight back, then pull forward to the left.
options.C: Pull straight forward, then drive straight back.

california.explanation: If you are asked to complete an offset back/left parking maneuver, you should first pull straight forward, then back up to the left. Your vehicle must be parked completely within the boundaries of the parking space.

california.question: As part of the vehicle inspection test, a CDL applicant may be asked to:
california.explanation: When checking the engine compartment during the vehicle inspection test, you will need to check the engine oil level.

california.question: A danger of swerving to avoid a hazard while driving a large truck is that:

options.A: The truck may miss the object.
options.C: The truck may stay in the same lane.

california.explanation: While swerving can sometimes be the safest way to handle a hazard on the roadway, doing so is not without risk. Top-heavy vehicles and tractors with multiple trailers may flip over in a swerve.

california.question: If the safety relief valve in the air brake system releases air:

options.B: There is something wrong with the brakes.

california.explanation: An air brake system has a safety relief valve, which releases air from the tanks if the pressure gets too high. If the valve must operate, something in the system is wrong and should be addressed by a mechanic.

california.question: Why should you regularly drain the air tanks?

options.A: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced
options.B: Because compressed air contains some water and the water collects in the tanks
options.C: To allow for a change in pressure

california.explanation: Compressed air usually contains a certain amount of moisture and compressor oil, which can build up in the air storage tanks and damage the brake system. The tanks should be drained to clean out these accumulations. On a tank with a manual drain valve, draining should be performed at the end of each day of driving.

california.question: When asked to make a lane change during the driving test, you should:

options.A: Make the change as soon as the examiner asks, without looking.
options.B: Use your turn signal and change lanes when safe.
options.C: Make the lane change as quickly as possible, even if that means cutting off another driver.

california.explanation: You will be asked to change lanes during the on-road driving test. When the examiner asks you to do this, you should make the necessary traffic checks and use the proper signals before changing lanes.

california.question: A cardboard box on the roadway:

options.A: Should be expected to be on the roadway.
options.C: Could contain a heavy object that could damage vehicles.

california.explanation: Almost any foreign object on the road poses some potential danger. For example, even something as seemingly harmless as a cardboard box could contain a hard or heavy object that could damage your vehicle.

california.question: When inspecting the windshield before a trip, a person should do all the following, except:

options.A: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
options.B: Check the windshield wipers for proper spring tension.
options.C: Check the wiper blades for damage.

california.explanation: When inspecting your windshield, you should look for cracks or other problems that could interfere with your ability to clearly see the road. The windshield wiper arms should be checked for proper spring tension. The wiper blades should be checked for damage, stiff rubber, and improper securement.

california.question: When inspecting your tires, you do not want to find:

options.A: Tire tread that is 4/32 of an inch deep.

california.explanation: There should be at least 4/32 of an inch of tread depth in every major groove on front tires and 2/32 of an inch on other tires. Valve stems should not be cut or cracked. Tire sizes should not be mismatched.

california.question: During a walk-around inspection, ensure there are no cracks on the brake drums that are more than ____ of the width of the friction area.
california.explanation: Before beginning a trip, it is important to check the brake drums during your walk-around inspection. It is unsafe to drive if any brake drum has a crack more than one half of the width of the friction area.

california.question: When accelerating on a surface with poor traction, such as a wet road, a driver should:

options.C: Not be concerned about the pavement.

california.explanation: You should accelerate very gradually when driving under conditions that create poor traction.

california.question: During the driving test, when asked to make a lane change:

options.A: You should not be concerned with other motorists.
options.B: You should use your turn signal and change lanes when safe.
options.C: You should make the lane change as quickly as possible, even if that means cutting off another driver.

california.explanation: When asked to make a lane change during the on-road driving test, you should make the proper traffic checks, use your turn signal, and smoothly change lanes when it is safe to do so.

california.question: A one-way check valve:

options.A: Drains the water and compressor oil from the air tanks.
options.B: Prevents air from escaping if the air compressor has a leak.
options.C: Activates the emergency brakes when there is a leak.

california.explanation: A one-way check valve is required to be between an air compressor and the first main reservoir. This valve prevents air from escaping the system if the air compressor develops a leak.

california.question: While driving, gauges are:

options.C: To be monitored for potential signs of trouble.

california.explanation: While driving, you should watch your vehicle's gauges for signs of trouble. Be sure to inspect your gauges before beginning a trip to ensure that they are in proper working order.

california.question: Who is responsible for cargo that has been loaded onto a truck?

options.A: The person who loaded the truck

california.explanation: Even if they did not load or secure the cargo themselves, the driver of a vehicle is responsible for inspecting the cargo and ensuring that it is properly secured.

california.question: A jogger wearing a stereo headset:

options.A: Is probably aware of what is happening around them.
options.B: May not be aware of what is happening around them.
options.C: Can hear the sounds of traffic.

california.explanation: Be careful around pedestrians, joggers, and cyclists who are wearing headphones. They may be unable to hear your vehicle approaching and may do dangerous things because they do not know you are there.

california.question: If an air compressor is belt-driven, the belt should be routinely checked to ensure that it is:
california.explanation: If your vehicle has air brakes, the air compressor drive belt should be checked before each drive. Check the tightness of the belt and verify that it is in good condition.

california.question: When starting an engine, oil pressure should come up to a normal level:
california.explanation: Look at your truck's gauges when starting the engine. The oil pressure in an engine should come up to a normal level within seconds of the vehicle's engine being started.

california.question: Your horn should be used to:

options.A: Tell other drivers that you are angry.
options.B: Warn other drivers that you are near.

california.explanation: Your vehicle's horn is a tool to warn others of your presence. Because the horn may create danger by startling other drivers, you should use it only if necessary.

california.question: Which of these sets of wheels will off-track the most?

options.B: It cannot be determined from the information given.

california.explanation: When any vehicle turns, its rear wheels will follow a shorter path than its front wheels. This is called off-tracking. The longer the vehicle, the greater the difference. In a combination vehicle, the trailer's wheels will off-track more than the tractor's rear wheels. In a double or triple combination vehicle, the wheels of the last trailer will off-track the most.

california.question: When pulling this type of trailer, you must be very careful at which of the following?
california.explanation: When pulling any trailer with low ground clearance, you must be careful to avoid getting stuck on raised ground such as a raised railroad crossing. Some lowboy trailers have as little as four inches of ground clearance. That may be insufficient to let you negotiate a roundabout without scraping and damaging the curbs or truck apron. Studies have shown that lowboy vehicles have problems negotiating curbs and truck aprons that are more than three inches high.

california.question: On your new tractor-trailer, you will find these two colored knobs on the dashboard. To release the vehicle’s parking brakes, you should
california.explanation: Newer vehicles with air brakes have a diamond-shaped yellow knob on the dashboard. When you pull the knob out, air is evacuated from the brake chambers, causing the spring brakes to come on. When you push the knob in, the parking brakes are released.

california.question: Which of the following trucks is likely to experience the strongest forward-and-backward surge?
california.explanation: Many tanker trucks have baffles to reduce forward-and-backward surge. However, regulations prohibit baffles when transporting foodstuffs such as milk because of the difficulty of keeping the tank interior clean. Drive such tanker trucks with extreme caution.

california.question: While uncoupling this semitrailer from the tractor, the driver has just disconnected the air and electrical lines. According to the official state CDL manual, what should the driver have done beforehand?

options.A: The driver should have eased pressure on the fifth wheel locking jaws.
options.B: The driver should have locked the trailer brakes.
options.C: The driver should have lowered the trailer's landing gear.
options.D: The driver should have performed all of the above steps.

california.explanation: The recommended uncoupling procedure in the official state CDL manual can be summarized as follows: (1) Position your vehicle. (2) Lock the trailer brakes and then ease pressure on the locking jaws. (3) Chock the trailer wheels unless you're sure that the trailer has spring brakes that work properly. (4) Lower the landing gear until it makes firm contact with the ground (plus a few extra turns for a loaded trailer). (5) Disconnect the air and electrical lines. (6) Unlock the fifth wheel. (7) Pull the tractor partially clear of the trailer. (8) Secure the tractor. (9) Inspect the trailer supports to be sure that the ground and the landing gear are supporting the trailer. (10) Pull the tractor completely clear of the trailer.

california.question: This vehicle is equipped with air drum brakes. To apply the drum brakes, which of the following forces the brake shoes against the lining of the brake drum?
california.explanation: This vehicle is equipped with S-cam air drum brakes. To apply the drum brakes, air is let into each brake chamber. Air pressure pushes the pushrod (A) out, moving the slack adjuster (B), thus rotating the brake camshaft. As the S-cam (C) on the camshaft rotates, it forces the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.

california.question: When the driver of a large CMV with air brakes presses the brake pedal, compressed air enters the control port of relay valves like this one. Where does this air go then?
california.explanation: The action of a relay valve is controlled by a piston inside it. When the brake pedal is pressed, compressed air from the foot valve enters the control port of the relay valve. This air is used only to activate the relay valve, not to fill the brake chambers. This air fills the small space at the top of the piston and pushes the piston downward. When the piston moves downward, air from air tanks connected to the relay valve's supply ports is allowed to flow through the valve to its delivery ports. From there, the air flows to the brake chambers to apply the brakes. Note: Relay valves come in many different models and shapes, though they all function similarly. The relay valves in your vehicle may well look different from the one shown here.

california.question: This is a diagram of a tractor-trailer's dual air brake system. In this scenario, the trailer has just accidentally broken away from the tractor, rupturing both air lines. Which valves will close automatically?
california.explanation: The trailer air supply valve ("red knob" control) and the tractor protection valve will act together to protect the tractor air supply from being depleted to an unsafe level. The sudden loss of air through the broken trailer supply line will cause the trailer air supply valve to close (and the eight-sided red knob on the dashboard to pop out). Because there is no pressure in the supply line to the trailer, the tractor protection valve will close also. Once the driver is aware of what is happening, he or she will almost certainly try to brake the tractor to a stop. There will be enough air to do this because the tractor protection valve will keep air from leaking out of the ruptured air lines.

california.question: In a vehicle equipped with air brakes, this type of valve is located under the brake pedal. In a typical combination vehicle with air brakes, when you depress the brake pedal, this valve lets compressed air flow to _________ in the trailer(s).
california.explanation: If compressed air had to flow directly from the foot valve to the trailer's brake chambers, there would be an unacceptably long time lag before the air would reach the brake chambers. Instead, relay valves are used on such large vehicles to speed up the braking process. Air from the foot valve quickly flows through narrow air lines (called control lines) to the relay valves. This air is used only as a signal to tell the relay valves to activate the brakes. Then the relay valves send air directly from air tanks to the brake chambers. The trailer may have its own air tank for this purpose.

california.question: Which of the following are considered NON-bulk packaging?
california.explanation: To qualify as non-bulk, a package must satisfy the following: 450 L (119 gallons) or less for liquids, 400 kg (882 pounds) or less and 450 L (119 gallons) or less for solids, and 454 kg (1,000 pounds) or less for gases. Under these requirements, choice A, an ordinary 55-gallon drum, would qualify as non-bulk packaging. The other two choices qualify as bulk packaging: B (intermediate bulk container - a portable, reusable container for liquids or solids. They are considered "intermediate" because they are typically smaller than portable tanks.) and C (T11 portable tank).

california.question: On a tractor-trailer equipped with air brakes, this coupler is used to connect
california.explanation: To keep the gladhand couplers and their corresponding air lines from being mismatched, they can be labeled with metal tags or color coded. Blue is used for the service lines, and red is used for the emergency lines. Couple the air lines of the same color. Green is often used to denote the electrical cables.

california.question: In this image of a leaf spring, what is the part marked "A" called?
california.explanation: A shackle attaches one end of a leaf spring to the vehicle frame. As the leaf spring flexes, its length changes and the shackle moves to allow for that. (The other end of the leaf spring is tightly mounted on the frame and cannot move.)

california.question: Which of the following placards is appropriate for a tanker truck carrying a cargo of gasoline?
california.explanation: Class 3 hazardous materials are flammable liquids such as gasoline. The class number (3) is on the Flammable Liquids placard.

california.question: If this converter dolly is equipped with antilock brakes (ABS), the dolly should have an ABS malfunction light

options.B: in any one of these locations.

california.explanation: Converter dollies built on or after March 1, 1998 are required to have antilock brakes. These dollies will also have a yellow ABS malfunction lamp on the left side.

california.question: Which of these helpers is best positioned to help this truck driver back up?
california.explanation: Position your helper where there’s a clear, continuous view of the backing path that your vehicle will follow and where you will be able to see the helper throughout the backing maneuver. In this case, helper C best meets these requirements.

california.question: What must you do if you are involved in a collision that involves death, injury, or property damage over $1,000?

options.A: Stop driving your vehicle for 10 days.
options.B: File an official report on form SR-1 within 10 days.

california.explanation: If any such incidents occur, you must file an official report, using Form SR-1, within 10 days. Your employer will have its own rules about company reporting and driving its trucks.

california.question: What is the gross vehicle weight (GVW)?

options.A: The total weight of the vehicle, including the load and any trailers
options.B: The total weight of a single vehicle and its load
options.C: A vehicle's maximum weight rating, specified by its manufacturer

california.explanation: GVW is the weight of a single vehicle plus the weight of the load that it is carrying.

california.question: Checking your vehicle's suspension does NOT include checking
california.explanation: Checking the suspension includes checking the springs, axles, shock absorbers, torque rods or arms, etc. The tires are on a different checklist.

california.question: Which of these is NOT a rule to follow for backing safely?

options.A: Make use of a helper as often as possible.
options.B: Combine backing and turning toward the driver's side whenever you can.
options.C: Accelerate slightly to complete the backing process quickly.
options.D: Back slowly while using your mirrors.

california.explanation: Backing safely involves taking it slowly: Look around, watch your path as well as your mirrors, and pay attention to your helper's signals. You should never have to accelerate while backing.

california.question: At what speed should you test the stopping action of the service brakes?
california.explanation: To test the stopping action of your service brakes, you should go at about 5 mph and press the brake pedal firmly. If the vehicle pulls to one side or stopping takes longer than normal, it could mean trouble.

california.question: What is the safest speed when you are driving in heavy traffic?

options.A: As fast as possible, to get out of the way
options.B: 15 mph below the speed of other traffic
options.D: The speed of other traffic (if not illegal or unsafe)

california.explanation: When you drive at the speed of other traffic, you do not have to constantly pass others or be passed by them, making collisions less likely. However, you should not attempt to keep up with drivers who drive faster than the speed limit for commercial motor vehicles (CMVs).

california.question: Which of these is NOT part of the basic method for shifting up?

options.A: Push in the clutch and shift into a higher gear at the same time.
options.B: Release the clutch and press the accelerator at the same time.
options.C: Accelerate while pressing the clutch and turning toward the driver's side.

california.explanation: You must release the accelerator, push in the clutch and shift into neutral at the same time, release the clutch, let the engine and gears slow to the required rpm for the next gear, push in the clutch and shift into a higher gear at the same time, then release the clutch and press the accelerator at the same time. Acceleration is not involved until the very end, and definitely not while pressing the clutch.

california.question: To help you stay alert and safe while driving, you should

options.A: have a whiskey to brace yourself.
options.B: roll down your windows to get fresh air.
options.C: avoid medications whose warning labels mention drowsiness.
options.D: drink coffee if you get drowsy.

california.explanation: Be careful with medications that warn you they may cause drowsiness. If you have a concern about prescribed medications, speak to your doctor. Do not try to fight sleepiness with coffee, fresh air, or especially alcohol. The only cure for feeling tired is sleeping until you are rested.

california.question: According to the Handbook, children present a hazard because

options.A: they don't know how to drive.
options.B: they often have grudges against truck drivers.
options.C: they don't know that trucks are dangerous.
options.D: they move quickly without checking traffic.

california.explanation: Most children allowed to play outside are old enough to understand the danger of large vehicles. Often, however, they do not check for traffic before running into the street.

california.question: Which of these should you NOT do during a drive wheel skid?
california.explanation: Hard braking could end up locking the drive wheels, possibly leading to a jackknife or total loss of control. Instead, ease off the accelerator and the brake pedal. Your vehicle should start to straighten out as the wheels regain traction. Steer gently to get back on course. You may find that your vehicle starts to skid in the opposite direction. In that case, steer quickly to counteract that skid (countersteer). Note: It's wise to practice this complicated maneuver before you get into an actual skid.

california.question: A top-heavy load is dangerous because it can cause

options.B: a rollover if you swerve around a hazard.
options.C: damage to the axles or steering.

california.explanation: A top-heavy load raises your vehicle's center of gravity so that you're much more likely to roll over on a curve or if you swerve to avoid a hazard. A top-heavy load is also an unbalanced load, which can damage certain parts of your vehicle, such as the axles.

california.question: Which of these are signs of a driver under the influence?

options.A: Difficulty maintaining his or her speed
options.B: Trouble staying in his or her own lane
options.C: Stopping suddenly for no apparent reason

california.explanation: Drivers under the influence tend to drive like a drunk friend at a party walks: They can't stay in their lane, they suddenly stop, and they slow down or speed up for no reason.

california.question: Which of these will cause you to lose your CDL for a minimum of one year for the first offense?

options.A: Refusing to undergo blood alcohol testing when asked to do so
options.B: Driving a commercial motor vehicle (CMV) when your blood alcohol content (BAC) is .04% or higher
options.C: Committing a felony that involves your use of a CMV

california.explanation: There are many reasons why you might lose your CDL for a year in California, including alcohol, crimes, and serious traffic violations such as hit and run.

california.question: Where should you place your warning devices, if you must stop on a one-way or divided highway?

options.A: 20 feet, 50 feet, and 100 feet toward approaching traffic
options.B: 50 feet, 100 feet, and 150 feet toward approaching traffic
options.C: 100 feet, 200 feet, and 300 feet toward approaching traffic
options.D: 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet toward approaching traffic

california.explanation: This is required by Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations Part 392.22, issued by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA). Those regulations also specify where to place warning devices on other types of roadways such as two-way roads and curves.

california.question: You don't want to be a distracted driver, so you

options.A: have all your emotionally difficult conversations in your first hour of driving.
options.B: read maps or use your phone only when there are no other vehicles around you.
options.C: smoke, eat, and drink on straight portions of the road.

california.explanation: A distraction is still a distraction, even on a straightaway or an empty road. Do not eat, drink, smoke, text, read, or have difficult conversations while driving. If possible, turn off your phone and keep it off until you are done driving for the day.

california.question: Legal maximum weight limits may not be safe in all of the following, EXCEPT
california.explanation: Maximum weight limits may not always be safe, especially in bad weather or steep mountain driving. Traffic is a fact of life, though.

california.question: Your vehicle is stuck on railroad tracks. You should

options.A: gather up your belongings and paperwork and then leave the cab.
options.B: immediately get out of the cab and move away from the tracks.
options.C: try to save some of the cargo if you don't see a train yet.
options.D: keep trying to move your vehicle until you see the train.

california.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, your safety comes first. Immediately leave the vehicle and get away. Do not risk your life to save belongings, paperwork, cargo, or even the vehicle.

california.question: Flags or lights are required on projecting loads that extend

options.A: 56 inches or more beyond the rear body.
options.B: 4 or more feet beyond the rear body.
options.C: 6 or more feet beyond the rear body.
options.D: 3 or more feet beyond the rear body.

california.explanation: A load that extends 4 feet or more beyond the rear body of the vehicle is considered a projecting load and thus requires a 12-inch-square red or fluorescent orange flag in the daytime and two lit red lights visible for 500 feet at night.

california.question: During a seven-step inspection, checking the engine compartment does NOT include checking

options.D: the coolant level in the radiator.

california.explanation: Checking your engine compartment consists of checking several fluid levels contained within. The oil pressure gauge is checked in a different step.

california.question: Can federal inspectors inspect your truck or bus?

options.B: Yes, but they will not place it out-of-service.
options.C: Yes, and they might place it out-of-service.

california.explanation: Federal or state inspectors may inspect your vehicle. If they find a problem that makes the vehicle potentially unsafe, they will put the vehicle out-of-service until the problem is fixed.

california.question: How does "bleeding tar" affect the road surface and driving conditions?

options.B: It is very sticky and slows down your vehicle.
options.C: It does not affect the road surface or driving conditions.

california.explanation: On hot days, tar in the pavement can rise to the surface and create a slippery film on the road surface.

california.question: How many reflective warning triangles must you carry with you for emergencies?
california.explanation: Your truck's emergency equipment must include warning devices such as three reflective red triangles, three liquid burning flares, or six fusees.

california.question: Cargo that can shift should have at least ____ tie-down(s).
california.explanation: The rule is one tie-down for every ten feet of cargo but at least two tie-downs regardless of how small the cargo is.

california.question: If you are found to have a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.02%, you will be placed out-of-service for
california.explanation: If your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is found to be 0.04% or more, you can be charged with driving under the influence (DUI). (An average 180-pound man may reach a BAC above 0.04% after drinking just two cans of beer.) Even if you are found to have any detectable amount of alcohol in your system under 0.04%, you will be placed out-of-service for 24 hours.

california.question: What are some advantages of going right instead of left around an obstacle?

options.A: Someone may be passing to the left.
options.B: You can avoid a head-on collision.
options.C: Both of the above are advantages.

california.explanation: Steering to the left of a hazard can cause you to move into the path of an oncoming vehicle or a vehicle that is trying to pass you on the left.

california.question: It takes the body about ____ hours to get rid of the alcohol in four alcoholic drinks.
california.explanation: The liver processes about one-third of an ounce of alcohol per hour, which is equivalent to at most one drink per hour.

california.question: While driving at highway speeds, you should look ahead
california.explanation: While driving, you should scan the road 12–15 seconds ahead. At 60 mph, your vehicle will travel a quarter of a mile in 15 seconds.

california.question: Name two situations in which the legal maximum weights may not be safe to haul.

options.C: During bad weather; in the mountains

california.explanation: A heavily loaded vehicle will have a longer stopping distance, and its speed will be harder to control on downgrades. Therefore, when you must travel in bad weather or in the mountains, consider keeping the load significantly below the maximum legal weight limit.

california.question: To prevent a load from shifting, there should be at least one tie-down for every ____ feet of cargo.
california.explanation: The rule is one tie-down for every ten feet of cargo but at least two tie-downs regardless of how small the cargo is.

california.question: When driving at night, use your low beams when an oncoming vehicle is within
california.explanation: To prevent blinding other drivers at night, dim your headlights to low beams whenever you are within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle or within 500 feet of a vehicle you are following.

california.question: It is illegal to drive a CMV if your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is ______ or above.
california.explanation: You will lose your CDL for at least one year if you are convicted of driving a CMV while your BAC is 0.04% or above.

california.question: What is the minimum tread depth for front tires?
california.explanation: Steering axle tires must have a tread depth of at least 4/32 inch. All other tires must have a tread depth of at least 2/32 inch.

california.question: What is black ice?

options.A: A thin layer of ice clear enough that you can see the road underneath it

california.explanation: Black ice is a thin layer of ice that is clear enough for you to see the road beneath. Black ice is treacherous because it makes the road only look wet, not icy.

california.question: What is the minimum tread depth for tires other than steering axle tires?
california.explanation: Steering axle tires must have a tread depth of at least 4/32 inch. All other tires must have a tread depth of at least 2/32 inch.

california.question: You must drive on a slippery road. Which of these is a good thing to do in such a situation?
california.explanation: Braking on a slippery surface can lock the wheels and cause a skid. Brake gently and slow down very gradually.

california.question: Which of these statements is true regarding the use of drugs while driving?

options.A: Prescription drugs are allowed as long as your doctor says the drugs will not affect safe driving ability.
options.B: No prescription or nonprescription drugs are allowed at any time for any reason.
options.C: "Speed" and other amphetamines are allowed as long as you are using the drugs to stay awake.

california.explanation: Some prescription drugs can impair your driving abilities. Take a prescription drug only if your doctor assures you that it won't impair your driving abilities.

california.question: Name some suspension system defects.

options.A: Broken leaves in a leaf spring and a cracked or broken spring hanger

california.explanation: Leaking shock absorbers and broken or missing leaves are two of the more common defects that may occur in a suspension system.

california.question: At a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______, most people lose consciousness, and some die.
california.explanation: Most people with a BAC of 0.40% will pass out and some will even die.

california.question: Which of these is especially true about your tires in hot weather?

options.A: If a tire is too hot to touch, you should hose it down with water.
options.B: You should bleed a small amount of air to keep tire pressure steady.
options.C: You should check tire mounting and air pressure before driving.

california.explanation: In hot weather, check the tire mounting and tire pressure carefully. Heat causes the air in the tire to expand, increasing tire pressure. Driving will make the tires even hotter. If the tire temperature and pressure rise too high, the tire may blow out or even catch fire.

california.question: What does "axle weight" mean?

options.A: The weight transmitted to the ground by one axle or one set of axles
options.B: The weight transmitted to the tires from the axle

california.explanation: Axle weight is the weight transmitted from one axle or a set of axles to the ground.

california.question: An en-route inspection should include checking

options.A: that the cargo is properly secured.
options.B: for tire overheating and brake overheating.

california.explanation: Whenever you stop during your trip, check whether the cargo has shifted. Also check whether the tires or brakes are overheating. Overheating could cause them to fail or even start a fire.

california.question: As part of your pre-trip inspection, you must check for
california.explanation: Regardless of who loads and secures the cargo, you, the driver, are responsible for its safety. As part of your pre-trip inspection, make sure that the cargo is balanced, secured, and not overloaded, and does not get in the way of emergency equipment. The cargo's safety could be compromised otherwise.

california.question: Why do dry bulk tanks require special care?

options.A: They have a high center of gravity.
options.C: Both of the above answers are correct.

california.explanation: It takes special skills to drive a tank truck. Dry bulk tanks have a high center of gravity and their loads can shift, making the vehicle more prone to rollovers. Use extreme caution on curves and when making sharp turns.

california.question: Underloaded front axles can cause
california.explanation: Cargo must be loaded to keep the weight of the vehicle properly balanced. If there's not enough weight over the front axle, the front tires won't have enough traction for the vehicle to be steered safely.

california.question: What should you do in thick fog?

options.A: Follow the taillights or headlights in front of you
options.B: Assume that the fog will thin out after you enter it
options.C: Pull off the road into a rest area or truck stop

california.explanation: You should watch for foggy conditions and be ready to reduce your speed. Do not assume that the fog will thin out after you enter it. The best advice for driving in fog is: don’t. It is preferable that you pull off the road into a rest area or truck stop until visibility is better. Watch for vehicles on the side of the roadway. Seeing taillights or headlights in front of you may not be a true indication of where the road is ahead of you. The vehicle may not be on the road at all.

california.question: What is the minimum tread depth for front (steering) tires?
california.explanation: Front steering tires require a tread depth of at least 4/32 inch. All other tires must have a tread depth of at least 2/32 inch.

california.question: Which of these is true about the radiator shutters and the winterfront?

options.A: You should remove ice from the radiator shutters.
options.B: The winterfront should be closed tightly.
options.C: The engine may overheat if the winterfront is left open.

california.explanation: In extremely cold weather, very cold air flowing onto the radiator and through the engine compartment can prevent the engine from warming up (and also keep your heater from working well). Radiator shutters or a winterfront restrict this air flow to let the engine warm up. However, don't overdo it. Keep the winterfront partially open or keep the radiator shutters free from ice. If the shutters freeze shut or the winterfront is closed too tightly, the engine may overheat from lack of sufficient air.

california.question: The amount of liquid to load into a tank depends on

options.B: the amount the liquid will expand in transit.

california.explanation: How much liquid you can load into a tank depends on the following: (1) Heat makes liquid expand, so you must allow enough room at the top of the tank for outage. (2) A dense liquid may weigh so much that loading too much liquid into the tank may cause your vehicle to exceed state weight limits.

california.question: Where should you keep the shipping papers?

options.A: In a pouch on the driver's door

california.explanation: Your life, and the lives of others, may depend on quickly locating the hazardous materials shipping papers. For that reason, you must identify shipping papers related to hazardous materials or keep them on top of other shipping papers. You must also keep shipping papers: in a pouch on the driver's door; or in clear view within reach while driving; or on the driver's seat when out of the vehicle.

california.question: You were forced to leave the road in an emergency, and you are forced to return to the road before stopping on the shoulder. What should you do?

options.A: Using mirrors and turn signals, turn sharply to get back onto the road.
options.B: Drive on the shoulder to the next exit and then re-enter the road.
options.C: Using mirrors and turn signals, edge gradually back onto the road.

california.explanation: If you've left the road but you must return to the road before stopping on the shoulder, the recommended recovery procedure is as follows: 1. Hold the wheel tightly and turn sharply enough to get right back onto the road safely. 2. Don't try to edge gradually back onto the road. If you do, your tires might grab unexpectedly and you could lose control. 3. When both front tires are on the paved surface, countersteer immediately. The two turns should be made as a single "steer-countersteer" move.

california.question: If your brakes fail on a downgrade, what should you do?

options.A: Wait until you find an escape ramp to exit the roadway.
options.B: Look outside your vehicle for another means of slowing down.
options.C: Hit some object in order to stop your vehicle.

california.explanation: If your brakes fail, first look for an escape ramp. If no escape ramp is readily available, take the least hazardous escape route you can – such as an open field or a side road that flattens out or turns uphill. Do this as soon as you discover that your brakes have failed. The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go, and the harder it will be to stop.

california.question: If you must cross into the oncoming lane as you make a right turn, you should

options.C: back up to allow oncoming traffic to pass.

california.explanation: To make a right turn, turn slowly to give yourself and others more time to avoid problems. If you must cross into the oncoming lane to make a turn, watch out for vehicles coming toward you. Give them room to go by or to stop. Don't back up for them, however, because you might hit someone behind you.

california.question: If you're not sure what to use to put out a hazardous materials fire, what should you do?
california.explanation: If you don't know how to put out the fire, you could end up making things even worse. In this case, you're better off calling professional firefighters to deal with the situation.

california.question: If you have to complete a vehicle inspection report, you must sign it

options.A: only when defects are noted that are certified to not need repair.
options.B: only when defects are noted that are certified to be repaired.

california.explanation: You may have to complete a vehicle inspection report in writing each day. The motor carrier must repair any items in the report that affect safety, and certify on the report that repairs were made or were unnecessary. You must sign the report only if defects were noted and certified to be repaired or not needed to be repaired.

california.question: Which of these would probably NOT help if your windshield becomes covered with ice?
california.explanation: In the wintertime, remove snow and ice from your windshield, windows, and mirrors before you drive.
